summary: Feed s160_double is degraded with 2 high-severity faults: 100% of packets missing required VLAN tags (10, 20) and 24.8% of TCP sessions are one-way (38/153). NDR requires both directions and VLAN context for full detection coverage.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker egress (or SPAN trunk) is stripping 802.1Q tags. 100% of packets arrived untagged while NDR requires VLANs 10 and 20, indicating broker port configured to remove tags, access-mode instead of trunk, or VLAN stripping policy enabled.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR loses network segmentation context for VLANs 10 and 20. Cannot apply VLAN-aware detection policies, correlate assets by segment, or detect lateral movement/VLAN hopping. Coverage for those segments is effectively blind.

recommended_fix.why: Configure packet broker and SPAN/TAP trunk ports to preserve 802.1Q tags on egress to the NDR tool port. Disable 'strip VLAN' and ensure trunk allows VLANs 10,20 so NDR receives tagged traffic as required.

findings.root_cause: Only one direction of bidirectional flows is delivered to the NDR. 38 of 153 TCP sessions (24.8% > 10% threshold) show single direction, typical of TAP/SPAN covering only one side of an asymmetric path or packet broker not aggregating RX/TX pair to the same tool port / splitting directions via hash.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR requires both directions (needs_both_directions=true) for TCP reassembly, session state tracking and behavioral detection. One-way traffic breaks flow reconstruction, causes missed detections, incomplete metadata, and false positives for the 24.8% affected sessions.

recommended_fix.why: Configure packet broker to aggregate both directions of each flow to the same NDR tool port using flow-aware/symmetric aggregation. Ensure TAPs on both sides of the conversation are combined, so client->server and server->client for the same session egress together.
